newsitem.title: USA: Andersen Worldwide nominee misses bid for post-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Andersen Worldwide nominee misses bid for post-WSJ.

text.p: The latest nominee to head Andersen Worldwide has failed to secure enough partner votes to take the post, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Thursday's electronic edition, the Journal said that George Shaheen, the second nominee put forth by the board, was unable to garner the necessary two-thirds vote of the firm's 2,700 partners.
Shaheen, the manager partner at Andersen Consulting, would have succeeded Lawrence Weinbach as Andersen Worldwide's managing partner and chief executive. Weinbach plans to step down on August 31.
Officials at Andersen, a professional services organization, would not disclose the tally.

This is the second time in less than two months that the board's choice to succeed Weinbach has been rejected by partners. Jim Wadia, the United Kingdom's managing partner for Arthur Andersen, also was unable to secure the two-thirds backing.
The Andersen Worldwide board is expected to meet Friday to discuss its next step.
